source_title: Richter's syndrome of the central nervous system diagnosed concurrently with chronic lymphocytic leukaemia: A case report and literature review
disease_label_per_paper: Richter syndrome of the CNS diagnosed concurrently with chronic lymphocytic leukemia
presentation_summary: Presented with slurred speech, headache, and left-sided hemiparesis
Brain MRI showed an irregular 30 mm lesion in the right parietal lobe
Admission blood tests showed WBC 22.2 x10^9/L and lymphocyte count 14.5 x10^9/L, with normal hemoglobin and platelet count
After tumor resection, pathology showed diffuse large B-cell lymphoma of non-germinal center type
Subsequent hematology evaluation showed no night sweats, fever, weight loss, lymph node enlargement, or hepatosplenomegaly; LDH was 155 IU/L with reference 120-250 IU/L
Blood and bone marrow flow cytometry supported CLL, CSF contained DLBCL cells, and IGH/IGK analysis indicated that the brain DLBCL was derived from the CLL clone
The patient received intravenous high-dose methotrexate and intrathecal chemotherapy, but CNS disease progressed and she died ten weeks after symptom onset

pathology.diagnosis: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, non-germinal center type

pathology.details: Blood FACS and bone marrow findings were consistent with CLL.

infection_exclusion_context.details: HIV testing was negative; no broader infectious exclusion panel was reported.

actual_treatment: Complete surgical resection of initial brain mass
Intrathecal methotrexate 10 mg, cytarabine 50 mg, and dexamethasone 5 mg
Planned radiotherapy could not be delivered because of clinical decline
Death occurred about ten weeks after symptom onset

outcome.source_text_value: died within a few days at just 10 weeks after the onset of symptoms

quality_warnings: Brain pathology, CLL flow cytometry, CSF FACS, and IGH/IGK clonal relation are stored as confirmatory/pathology evidence and are not ordinary observations.
This case is an unusual CNS-only Richter syndrome with no lymphadenopathy or hepatosplenomegaly on enhanced CT.
The fatal course is stored under outcome and is not used as ordinary diagnostic evidence.
